PNN-005 Hung out to dry. Forensics declined.

Pyro Posse airs the dirty laundry. Then sets it on fire.

In one night, the Pyro Posse hung scorched underwear on the Tightie Whities, a mystery clothesline on the Silver Bullets, and cobwebs on a house with a For Sale sign. They then posted the photos before the victims got home, deleted them, and announced that nobody else is playing. PNN has questions. Mostly about the underwear.

Subject team
Pyro Posse
Opened
October 10, 2026 at 5:30 PM (America/Denver)
PNN threat rating
Extra crispy. Zero surprises kept.

The incident

On the night of October 9, 2026, the Pyro Posse went on a laundry run. While two households were away at football games, the Posse visited the Tightie Whities and the Silver Bullets. For the Tightie Whities, a team named after underwear, the Posse selected the most obvious prank in the history of the neighborhood: underwear. On a clothesline. Out front. Then they set it on fire. PNN's legal desk calls this 'asking for it.' PNN's editorial desk calls it 'a gift.'

The result, PNN reports with a straight face, is a pair of scorched satin bloomers that are neither tight nor, any longer, white. The charring runs down the middle in a pattern PNN's forensic desk describes as 'unfortunately suggestive,' and which the Posse's own banner, hanging on the same line, calls 'The Skidmark Synod.' PNN did not choose that name. PNN did not need to. One must wonder whether fire was the only thing applied to these garments. PNN has not asked, and would prefer not to receive the answer in writing. The Posse's statement on the matter: 'The Whitie Tighties, a little distracted, have issues a little embarrassing to discuss. Under a little heat it took on apocalyptic levels. They were torched beyond repair thanks to the 🔥 PYRO POSSE 🔥!!' (The Posse also flipped the team name, which is a bold choice for a group that was just praised for precision.)

At the Silver Bullets, the Posse strung up something else. PNN has studied the photographs for an unreasonable amount of time and can classify the items only as 'laundry-adjacent': a yellow clothesline of charred blue bundles, clothespinned in a neat row, over a lawn dotted with paper flames and small white fragments of unknown origin. The Silver Bullets' home also has a flagpole, per PNN's source. A flagpole. The one structure on earth built to hoist things where the whole neighborhood can see them. The Posse used the low line instead and left the flagpole unemployed. The Posse issued no statement about this prank. The objects have not issued one either.

The same night, the Posse also pranked a third household, the Black Webb Bandits, and then forgot to mention it. The announcement did not arrive until late on October 10, the following day, possibly because the Posse was worried about announcing the other pranks too soon. The target: a home with a For Sale sign out front. The Posse draped the sign in orange cobweb, scattered orange flags and pumpkin-faced stakes across the lawn, and left. Their statement: 'The Pyro Posse were torching their way through the neighborhood and found some spiders who got caught in an orange webb of woe, a complete crape paper trap of catastrophe. And had to raise the orange flag of surrender because of the Pyro Posse. ☄️🔥☄️🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥 They couldn’t 🧯the power of the Pyro Posse.' PNN notes that the number of actual flames at the Bandits' house was zero, which makes it the first torching ever conducted entirely with crepe paper. Also, PNN got to the 'webb' pun first, in PNN-001, and will accept royalties in the form of silence. Priced to move. Staged to scare. Showings by appointment. Bring a lint roller.

Previously on the PNN desk: PNN-004 — Pyro Posse sets Area 51 Bureau ablaze. Fire department stands down.

Suspected motive

PNN theory: the Pyro Posse believe the game is a sprint. By their own count they have now pranked three teams (PNN counts four, because the Posse forgot one) and posted to the game group: 'It’s like we’re the only ones playing 🤷‍♀️'. This is what leading looks like when you start before the gun and everybody else is still tying their shoes. It is also what peaking in week one looks like. By the time of the final-night Halloween party, an October 9 prank will have the shelf life of a carved pumpkin on a warm porch. The Posse is already working on the sequel to a movie nobody will remember seeing.

Their second theory is that a prank is complete when the victim finds out. The Posse upgraded this to 'when everybody finds out, sooner.' Photos of the pranks were posted to the game group before the pranked households got home, spoiling the surprise for the people it was meant for and delivering it, free of charge, to everyone else. The photos were deleted quickly. Many people had already seen them. A Posse member explained: 'Sometimes I am fast…. Usually when I shouldn’t be.' PNN has no further questions and is considering the sentence for a plaque.

How did the Posse know the pranked households would be out at football games? PNN has opened an inquiry. Suspects include: a schedule, a calendar, Purrveillance, and the possibility of phone tapping, which PNN raises purely as a joke and adds that no phone was tapped and the only lines involved were clotheslines. Clueso demands a full audit of the Posse's intelligence budget, which PNN suspects consists of a clipboard and a group chat.

The Posse also arrived too early with two announcements and too late with a third, which in PNN-002 was the Black Webb Bandits' exact specialty. PNN theorizes that it is contagious. Patient zero is wearing black and has a webb.

Investigator's note

Clueso resents the claim that the Pyro Posse are the only team playing. The Prowling Purrpetrators are playing. They are simply not being caught, which Clueso regards as an advanced technique and a personal insult. He also notes, with professional envy, that the Posse knew exactly when two households would be away at football games, which suggests either excellent Purrveillance or a calendar. Clueso has requested the Posse's sources. He would like to compare them to his own, which currently consist of a dog-walker and a hunch.

Official PNN assessment

PNN assessment: four teams hit, three of them in one night, one of them forgotten until the following day. The Pyro Posse have burned laundry, spoiled surprises, deleted the evidence, and announced that nobody else is playing, a feat of confidence rarely seen outside a fire drill. The Tightie Whities are now officially a laundry matter. The Silver Bullets are officially unidentified. The Black Webb Bandits are officially listed, subject to inspection.

PNN reminds all teams that actual fire is not part of the game, that Rule 5 prohibits damaging property, and that the correct amount of fire for a prank is a paper cutout on a stick. PNN trusts the underwear was the Posse's to burn and that the lawn's only injury was to its pride.

Final ruling: the Posse came, they saw, they posted, and then they deleted, in that order, before the victims got home. They can start a fire. They cannot keep a secret. They cannot keep a count. Ashes pending appeal.
